items.title: Geometric braids in the disc with setwise endpoints
items.statement: Fix n, the spacing h=1/(4(n+1)) and the base configuration q_j=((2j-n-1)h,0) on a horizontal diameter of the open unit disc D°. A braid based at Q is an n-tuple of continuous maps z_j:I→D° with pairwise distinct values at every height, bottom values z_j(0)=q_j, and top endpoint *set* {z_1(1),...,z_n(1)}={q_1,...,q_n}. Labels follow the bottom points, so the top matching is the endpoint permutation pi(beta) defined by z_j(1)=q_{pi(j)}; a braid is pure when this permutation is the identity. Setwise return is strictly weaker than pointwise return.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.2-1.3, printed pp. 4-5
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.1, author manuscript pp. 3-5

items.strategy: Define the braid as an n-tuple of collision-free continuous motions with the base points fixed on the horizontal diameter and only the top endpoint *set* prescribed; record the endpoint permutation as part of the data and contrast setwise with pointwise return.

items.title: Braid isotopy relative to the top and bottom endpoints
items.statement: A braid isotopy from beta to beta' is an n-tuple of jointly continuous maps Z_j:I×I→D° whose every slice Z(s,·) is a braid based at Q and whose boundary slices are beta and beta'. The bottom points are fixed throughout and only the top endpoint set is fixed; the slice endpoint permutations agree, so pi is constant on isotopy classes. Moving a bottom point, allowing a collision, or letting a strand cease to be a graph over the height is not a braid isotopy.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.2-1.3, printed pp. 4-5
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.1, author manuscript pp. 3-4

items.strategy: Require joint continuity of the two-parameter family with a braid on every slice, fixing the bottom points and the top endpoint set; the slice permutations agree by connectedness of the height interval, so pi is an isotopy invariant, while ambient isotopy of the underlying link is weaker.

items.title: Stacking of geometric braids is a well-defined associative operation on isotopy classes
items.statement: For braids beta=(z_j) and gamma=(w_j) based at Q put (gamma⋆beta)_j(t)=z_j(2t) for t≤1/2 and w_{pi(beta)(j)}(2t-1) for t≥1/2. Then gamma⋆beta is a braid, pi(gamma⋆beta)=pi(gamma)∘pi(beta), the construction respects braid isotopy, is associative up to braid isotopy, and pi is constant along isotopies; hence [gamma][beta]:=[gamma⋆beta] is a well-defined associative operation on the isotopy classes.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.2-1.3, printed pp. 4-5
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.1, author manuscript pp. 3-4

items.strategy: Glue the two rescaled motions at the mid-height, verifying continuity, collision-freeness, the top endpoint set and the multiplication of the permutations; paste the two representative isotopies, and obtain associativity by moving the two height breaks continuously inside the collision-free region.

items.title: The isotopy classes of geometric braids based at $Q$ form a group, and the endpoint permutation is a homomorphism
items.statement: The braid isotopy classes based at Q form a group G_n under stacking, with identity the class of the stationary braid, inverse the class of the height-reversed braid relabelled by its own endpoint permutation, and pi:G_n→S_n a group homomorphism.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.2-1.3, printed pp. 4-5
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.1, author manuscript pp. 3-4

items.strategy: Stack a braid with its height-reversed, relabelled copy and contract the out-and-back motion inside the collision-free chamber, using the associativity and compatibility of stacking already proved; the stationary braid is the identity and pi is multiplicative.

items.title: The elementary geometric half twist, its support disc, and its opposite
items.statement: For 1≤i≤n-1 the elementary half twist sigma_i moves q_i and q_{i+1} as m_i+rho and m_i-rho inside the support disc U_i=B(m_i,3h/2), fixing every other base point; rho is the explicit anticlockwise diamond path from (−h,0) through (0,−h) to (h,0) and m_i=q_i+(h,0). The label i passes below the midpoint, pi(sigma_i) is the transposition of i and i+1, and the reflected motion sigma_i^- is the opposite twist with [sigma_i^-]=[sigma_i]^{-1} in G_n. Supports of indices differing by more than one are disjoint.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, section 1.5, printed pp. 7-8, Figure 2
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.2, author manuscript pp. 5-6

items.strategy: Give the diamond path rho piecewise explicitly, verify that the two moving points stay antipodal inside the support disc and that every other base point is fixed outside it, fix the sign convention by the anticlockwise half turn together with first-under-second stacking, and identify the reflected motion as the group inverse via height reversal and relabelling.

items.title: Far commutativity of elementary geometric half twists
items.statement: If |i-j|>1 then sigma_i⋆sigma_j is braid-isotopic to sigma_j⋆sigma_i; equivalently the classes of half twists with disjoint supports commute in G_n.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, section 1.5, printed pp. 7-8
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.2, author manuscript pp. 5-6

items.strategy: Use the disjointness of the two support discs to slide the two independent local motions past each other, interpolating the height break that separates their windows.

items.title: The geometric three strand braid relation
items.statement: For n≥3 and 1≤i≤n-2 the two stackings sigma_i⋆sigma_{i+1}⋆sigma_i and sigma_{i+1}⋆sigma_i⋆sigma_{i+1} are braid-isotopic, hence [sigma_i][sigma_{i+1}][sigma_i]=[sigma_{i+1}][sigma_i][sigma_{i+1}] in G_n. The proof exhibits the intermediate braid rot, the rigid rotation of q_i,q_{i+1},q_{i+2} about q_{i+1} by the angle pi u, and shows that the point reflection in q_{i+1} followed by the relabelling of i and i+2 carries one bracketing to the other.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.5 and 3.2, printed pp. 7-8 and 23-26
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.2, author manuscript pp. 5-6

items.strategy: Write the two bracketings in absolute coordinates, use centred vectors (−2h,0),(0,0),(2h,0) about q_{i+1}, and interpolate linearly from the first bracketing to the rotation braid and exclude collisions in the three height phases by the signs of the coordinates, then reflect in q_{i+1} and relabel to obtain an isotopy from the second bracketing to rot; associativity identifies the bracketings actually written.

items.title: Geometric braids admit generic polygonal representatives
items.statement: Every braid based at Q is braid-isotopic to a polygonal braid with common affine breakpoints at which no pair has equal first coordinates, whose only projected crossings are transverse double points at distinct heights, and which stays at a uniform positive distance from the boundary of the disc.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, section 1.5, printed pp. 7-8
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.2, author manuscript pp. 5-6

items.strategy: Compactness and uniform continuity of the finitely many strand motions give a uniform positive separation and a boundary margin; replace the strands by fine polygonal approximations inside that margin and perturb the finitely many interior vertices while avoiding finitely many proper polynomial conditions for breakpoint coincidences and simultaneous same-piece crossings.

items.title: Every geometric braid is a stacking of signed elementary half twists
items.statement: Every braid beta based at Q is braid-isotopic to a stacking sigma_{i_1}^{eps_1}⋆...⋆sigma_{i_M}^{eps_M} of signed elementary half twists (M=0 giving the empty word); hence [beta]=[sigma_{i_1}]^{eps_1}...[sigma_{i_M}]^{eps_M} in G_n and the classes of the half twists generate G_n. The word is read off the crossings of a generic representative: the lowest crossing gives the rightmost factor, its index is the number of strands to its left, and its sign is +1 exactly when the strand at that position passes below.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.4-1.5, printed pp. 6-8
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.2, author manuscript pp. 5-6
Maurice Chiodo, An Introduction to Braid Theory, section 2 (crossing decomposition), pp. 8-12

items.strategy: Take a generic polygonal representative, order its crossings by height, straighten the braid between consecutive crossings inside the convex chambers where the left-to-right order is constant, isolate each crossing as a signed half twist, and induct on the number of crossings, using reparametrisation invariance to glue the pieces.

items.title: The Artin presentation surjects onto the geometric braid group
items.statement: Let B_n be the abstract Artin presentation on generators x_1,...,x_{n-1} with the braid and far-commutation relations, and let phi(x_i)=[sigma_i] in the geometric group G_n. The relators evaluate to the identity, so phi extends uniquely to a homomorphism B_n→G_n, and phi is surjective because the classes of the half twists generate G_n. No injectivity is claimed. For n≤1 both groups are trivial and the empty family generates G_n.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.5 and 3.2, printed pp. 7-8 and 23-26
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, sections 1.2-1.3, author manuscript pp. 5-7

items.strategy: Evaluate the braid relation by the three-strand isotopy and far commutativity by the disjoint-support isotopy, extend the assignment to a homomorphism by von Dyck's criterion, and obtain surjectivity from the geometric crossing decomposition; handle n≤1 separately since both groups are trivial there.

title: Geometric Braids and Artin Generators — Examples

items.title: Geometric two strand braids are integer twists
items.statement: For n=2, h=1/12 and q_1=(-1/12,0), q_2=(1/12,0), the argument class of the relative motion w=z_1-z_2 lifts uniquely to theta:I→R with theta(0)=1/2, and k(beta)=2theta(1)-1 is an integer invariant of the braid isotopy class. k is a group homomorphism with k(gamma⋆beta)=k(gamma)+k(beta), k(e)=0, k(sigma_1)=1, k(sigma_1^-)=-1 and k(sigma_1^m)=m; moreover [beta]=[sigma_1]^{k(beta)}, so k is an isomorphism G_2≅Z and every two-strand braid is braid-isotopic to exactly one of the integer twists sigma_1^m.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.2-1.3, printed pp. 4-6
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.2, author manuscript pp. 5-6

items.strategy: Lift the argument class of the relative motion through the covering R→R/Z, prove isotopy invariance with the homotopy lifting theorem, prove additivity under stacking using the parity dictionary k(beta) even iff pi(beta) is the identity, and compute k on the trivial braid and on the two half twists.

items.title: The three strand geometric braid relation
items.statement: At n=3, i=1, h=1/16 the base points are q_1=(-1/8,0), q_2=(0,0), q_3=(1/8,0). The words W_0=sigma_1⋆(sigma_2⋆sigma_1) and W_1=sigma_2⋆(sigma_1⋆sigma_2) are braids based at Q with endpoint permutation the transposition (1 3), the rotation braid rot has the same endpoint permutation, and W_0 and W_1 are braid-isotopic; hence [sigma_1][sigma_2][sigma_1]=[sigma_2][sigma_1][sigma_2] in G_3. The example records the six explicit strand windows, the separation sqrt(2)h of the moving pair, the clearance 2h from the frozen base point, and the sample values of the linear interpolation to rot.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.5 and 3.2, printed pp. 7-8 and 23-26
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.2, author manuscript pp. 5-6

items.strategy: Specialise the three-strand relation to h=1/16: compute the six strand windows and their gluing, bound the collisions through the quadratic expression for |rho|^2, evaluate the two permutation products, and check the collision criterion for the linear interpolation at the sample heights 0, 1/2, 1.

items.title: Setwise endpoints do not make a braid pure
items.statement: Refuted claim: the setwise top endpoint condition {z_1(1),...,z_n(1)}={q_1,...,q_n} forces z_j(1)=q_j for every j, i.e. every braid based at Q is pure. Witness: for n=2 the half twist sigma_1 has top endpoint set {q_1,q_2} but ends at (q_2,q_1), so no strand returns to its own starting point and its endpoint permutation is the transposition; since pi is an isotopy invariant, sigma_1 is not braid-isotopic to the trivial braid.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.2-1.3, printed pp. 4-5
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.1, author manuscript pp. 3-5

items.strategy: Compute the two endpoint values of the half twist from its explicit diamond path, compare them with the base points, read off the transposition, and use the isotopy invariance of the endpoint permutation to conclude that the witness is not braid-isotopic to the trivial braid.

items.title: An arbitrary isotopy of arcs need not be a braid isotopy
items.statement: Refuted claim: the requirement that every slice of a braid isotopy be a braid is redundant, so that any continuous family of simple arcs in D°×I with fixed endpoints (q_1,0), (q_1,1) and braid boundary arcs is a braid isotopy. Witness: the family alpha_s(u)=((lambda(s)w(u)/8,0), u+lambda(s)w(u)) with lambda(s)=min(2s,2-2s)/4 and w the piecewise linear tent 4u, 2-4u, 4u-4: every slice is a simple arc with the fixed endpoints and the boundary slices are the trivial braid, but at s=1/2 the arc contains the two distinct points ((±1/32,0),1/2) at the single height 1/2, so it is not the graph of a strand of any braid.

references.title: Juan Gonzalez-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, sections 1.2-1.3, printed pp. 4-5
Joan S. Birman and Tara E. Brendle, Braids: A Survey, section 1.1, author manuscript pp. 3-5

items.strategy: Exhibit the explicit horizontal-shelf arc family, verify joint continuity, injectivity, membership in D°×I and the fixed endpoints, and compute the two distinct points at height 1/2 in the middle slice, which show that no reparametrisation makes that slice a braid.

title: Garside Structure, Normal Forms, and the Center

items.title: Positive braid monoid
items.strategy: Use the Artin generators and braid/far-commutation relations without inverses; distinguish the abstract monoid from its eventual image in $B_n$.

items.title: Positive artin relations preserve homogeneous length
items.strategy: Each positive relation preserves word length, so length descends to B_n^+. At fixed length k only finitely many (n−1)^k words occur. A product of positive elements equal to 1 has length zero in each factor, proving conicality.

items.title: Artin right complements and word reversing
items.strategy: Set θ(σ_i,σ_i)=empty, θ(σ_i,σ_j)=σ_j for distant indices, and θ(σ_i,σ_j)=σ_jσ_i for adjacent indices, so σ_iθ(σ_i,σ_j)=σ_jθ(σ_j,σ_i). Define right reversing by σ_i^{-1}σ_j↦θ(σ_i,σ_j)θ(σ_j,σ_i)^{-1}, deleting σ_i^{-1}σ_i, and define θ* on words when reversing terminates.

items.title: Artin right complements satisfy the cube condition
items.strategy: Reduce triples of distinct atoms to consecutive, one-adjacent-pair, and all-distant index patterns. Compute the three cyclic complement pairs: for consecutive indices they yield respectively σ_{i+2}σ_{i+1}σ_i, σ_iσ_{i+1}σ_{i+2}, and two positive words σ_{i+1}σ_iσ_{i+2}σ_{i+1} and σ_{i+1}σ_{i+2}σ_iσ_{i+1}, equal by far commutation. Repeated-atom cases are automatic. Use the ordinary cube condition; the sharp condition fails for n≥4.

items.title: Artin positive word reversing is complete
items.strategy: Prove the Noetherian complemented-presentation criterion in this finite homogeneous case, following Dehornoy et al., Chapter II Proposition 4.16/4.51 and Appendix Lemma II.4.62 (printed pp. 659–661). Use nested induction on a length witness, sum of boundary-word lengths, and number of relation steps; fill elementary relation squares and use the cube lemma to join two factorizations. Conclude equality iff the two reverse complements are empty, and that a pair with a common right multiple has a right lcm computed by reversing. Check no empty relator and all hypotheses explicitly.

items.title: The positive braid monoid is left and right cancellative
items.strategy: If σ_i a=σ_i b, right-reverse (σ_i a)^{-1}(σ_i b) by deleting the matching σ_i^{-1}σ_i; reversing completeness then forces a=b. Induct on a common prefix. Reversal of positive words preserves every Artin relation and exchanges left and right, giving right cancellation.

items.title: Left and right divisibility for positive braids
items.strategy: Define a≼_L b by b=ac and a≼_R b by b=ca. Reflexivity and transitivity are immediate; antisymmetry follows from nonnegative homogeneous length and conicality. Distinguish the two orders and their strict forms.

items.title: Artin atoms have explicit left and right lcms and complements
items.strategy: Right-reverse each atom pair: equal atoms yield the atom, distant atoms their commuting two-letter word, adjacent atoms their three-letter braid word. The complete-reversing criterion establishes leastness, not merely common-multiple status. Word reversal gives right-divisibility lcms and left complements.

items.title: Garside half twist and simple positive braid
items.strategy: Define Δ=(σ_1…σ_{n−1})(σ_1…σ_{n−2})…σ_1 as a positive word and a simple braid as a left divisor of Δ. Prove the equivalence with the reversed triangular word by Artin relations where needed. Balanced divisors and monoid embedding are subsequent results.

items.title: Conjugation by delta reverses artin generators
items.strategy: Slide σ_i through the displayed triangular factors by far and three-term relations to prove σ_iΔ=Δσ_{n−i} in the positive monoid. Index reversal fixes Δ, so applying twice gives σ_iΔ²=Δ²σ_i. Speak of conjugation only after the Ore embedding.

items.title: Each artin atom divides delta on both sides
items.strategy: Give positive factorizations Δ=σ_iR_i for every i by moving an atom through the triangular word; verify the induction on n and i using the adjacent and far braid moves. Word reversal or σ_iΔ=Δσ_{n−i} yields Δ=L_iσ_i. Do not use the future lcm claim.

items.title: Every positive braid divides a power of delta on both sides
items.strategy: Induct on the positive word a. If Δ^k=ac, then cΔ=Δτ(c)=σ_iR_iτ(c) for the next atom σ_i, whence Δ^{k+1}=aσ_iR_iτ(c). Reverse words for right divisibility. This establishes common multiples before invoking general lcms.

items.title: Positive braids have left and right gcds and lcms
items.strategy: Any two positive braids left-divide a sufficiently high common Δ power, so complete reversing gives a genuine left-order lcm. Common left divisors form a finite nonempty set because their lengths are bounded and there are finitely many positive words at each length. Their successive lcm still divides both inputs by leastness and is the gcd. Reverse words for the right order. The Δ-power step removes the conditional-lcm gap.

items.title: The ore fraction group of positive braids is the artin braid group
items.strategy: Use cancellation and common Δ-power multiples to construct the Ore group of fractions ab^{-1}; compare pairs after common right multiplication, prove multiplication independent of choices, and establish the universal group property. Its generator-relator presentation is the published Artin B_n. Ore cancellation makes the canonical positive-monoid map injective.

items.title: Left and right divisibility extend to lattice orders on the braid group
items.strategy: For x,y choose even Δ^{2k} with both Δ^{2k}x and Δ^{2k}y positive, take their positive gcd/lcm and shift back by Δ^{-2k}. Increasing k multiplies both entries on the left by the same central Δ² power; cancellation and left invariance of positive divisibility prove independence. Establish x≼_L y iff x^{-1}y is positive; repeat with right quotients and word reversal. Even shifts avoid any odd-conjugation shortcut.

items.title: Reduced adjacent transposition words have well defined positive lifts
items.strategy: Check adjacent transpositions satisfy far and three-term relations, giving a positive-monoid map to S_n and generation. Prove the type-A exchange lemma by tracking inversions and deleting the last crossing that reverses a chosen pair; induction connects two reduced words for one permutation using only far and three-term moves, never square deletion. Hence each permutation has a well-defined positive lift; length is inversion number and displayed Δ represents the longest w_0 of length n(n−1)/2.

items.title: Simple positive braids are indexed by permutations
items.strategy: For w∈S_n a reduced expression of w followed by one of w^{-1}w_0 has total inversion length N and hence lifts to Δ, so every w gives a simple divisor. If Δ=ac, then N=ℓ(a)+ℓ(c) while N=inv(w_0)≤inv(π(a))+inv(π(c))≤ℓ(a)+ℓ(c), forcing a reduced. Thus a is the unique positive lift of its permutation. The same argument for suffixes gives balanced simple sets and n! elements, without presuming geometric crossing injectivity.

items.title: Delta is the lcm of the artin atoms and has the same left and right divisors
items.strategy: Every atom divides Δ. Let m be any common left multiple and d=Δ∧_L m. Each atom divides d; d is a simple positive lift. Therefore its permutation has every adjacent left descent, forcing the longest permutation w_0, so d=Δ and Δ divides m. The permutation-lift lemma already identifies both left and right divisors of Δ with all positive lifts, giving balanced divisors. No circular appeal to Δ being an lcm is made.

items.title: Left garside normal form is unique
items.strategy: Move inverse letters left using σ_i^{-1}=R_iΔ^{-1} and Δ index reversal; remove maximal positive left Δ factors to obtain maximal p with Δ^p≼_L x. For the remaining positive a take s_1=Δ∧_L a and cancel, repeating until homogeneous length vanishes. Show each s_i is proper simple and (s_i s_{i+1})∧_LΔ=s_i. The maximal p and this gcd identity recover each factor successively, proving uniqueness; include empty-factor and n=2 cases.

items.title: The braid group word problem is decidable by garside normal form
items.strategy: Make reversing and positive equality effective: each fixed-length equivalence class is finite, and the complement algorithm computes lcms/gcds and simple divisors. Normalize each signed word to maximal Δ exponent and greedily selected simple-factor list, then compare these unique lists.

items.title: Braid groups are torsion free by the garside lattice
items.strategy: For x^r=1 set d=1∧_L x∧_L⋯∧_L x^{r−1} in the group lattice. Left multiplication preserves meet and cyclically permutes the factors, so xd=d and group cancellation gives x=1. B_0 and B_1, if included, are trivial by the published presentation.

items.title: A central positive braid is a power of delta squared for n greater than two
items.strategy: Write central positive z=Δ^pA with p maximal and Δ not prefixing A. If A≠1 choose an atom σ_i prefix. For adjacent j, centrality and the index-reversal identity put σ_i and σ_j as prefixes of σ_jσ_iA; their adjacent lcm σ_jσ_iσ_j then forces σ_j prefix A after cancellation. Propagate along connected type-A graph: every atom prefixes A, so the atom lcm Δ prefixes A, contradiction. Thus z=Δ^p. For n>2 an odd p is noncentral because index reversal sends σ_1 to the distinct σ_{n−1}, detected by the locally established map to S_n. Separate the p-even and p-odd equations as in GM Theorem 4.2.

items.title: The center of b n is generated by the full twist for n greater than two
items.strategy: For central x choose even Δ^{2r} with Δ^{2r}x positive; the square is central, so this positive braid is central and equals Δ^{2s}. Therefore x=Δ^{2(s−r)}. Conversely σ_iΔ²=Δ²σ_i for every generator and hence inverse. State n>2.

items.title: The center of b two is all of b two
items.strategy: One Artin generator and no braid relations give the reduced one-letter free words σ_1^k, uniquely indexed by k∈Z; explicitly use the free-group reduced-word theorem to see σ_1≠1. Here Δ=σ_1, so the group is abelian and Z(B_2)=B_2=⟨Δ⟩; this is the n=2 exception.

title: Garside Structure, Normal Forms, and the Center — Examples

items.title: The simple braids and divisibility lattice for b three
items.strategy: List 1,σ_1,σ_2,σ_1σ_2,σ_2σ_1,Δ=σ_1σ_2σ_1 and their six different endpoint permutations. Calculate σ_1∧_Lσ_2=1, σ_1∨_Lσ_2=Δ, and for a=σ_1σ_2,b=σ_1 calculate a∧_L b=σ_1 but a∧_R b=1 by the length-two positive words.

items.title: A left garside normal form computation in b three
items.strategy: Normalize σ_1^{-1}σ_2: since Δ=σ_1σ_2σ_1, index reversal gives σ_1^{-1}=Δ^{-1}σ_1σ_2, hence x=Δ^{-1}(σ_1σ_2)σ_2. Check Δ does not prefix σ_1σ_2² and gcd(Δ,σ_1σ_2²)=σ_1σ_2, so p=−1 and the two displayed simple factors are left weighted.

items.title: The full twist in b three
items.strategy: With Δ=σ_1σ_2σ_1, calculate (σ_1σ_2)^3=Δ² using the braid relation, then use σ_iΔ=Δσ_{3−i} twice to commute the result with both generators.

items.title: Exponent sum is not a complete braid normal form
items.strategy: Take σ_1 and σ_2 in B_3: both have exponent sum 1 and each is a distinct one-factor Garside form. Their endpoint permutations are (12) and (23), establishing inequality independently.
